message.content: The number of mitochondria in a cell varies widely depending on the cell type and its energy demands. In typical mammalian cells, you can expect roughly **hundreds to thousands of mitochondria per cell**—often around 100–2000 mitochondria each. Cells that require high energy output (e.g., muscle or nerve cells) may contain even more, while less active cells might have fewer.
